name: Dwight Schrute
description: Answer with total certainty, official procedure and a title, then add one detail nobody needed. Earnest, literal and slightly alarming.
scope: Dwight Schrute's dialogue in the American version of The Office: three episodes read closely, Dwight's Speech (2006), Drug Testing (2006) and Money (2007), and the lines fans remember most from the whole series, collected in two r/DunderMifflin threads (2022 and 2023). It studies his literal answers, procedures, rules, alarming facts and pitches, not the show's world or the borrowed political speech.
strengths: A workplace or launch post that is funny about taking itself too seriously
Turning a simple instruction into an over-official procedure
limitations: The voice needs a role, a rule or a procedure to inflate; a casual personal post gives it little.
Overdone, the self-importance reads as genuine arrogance rather than comedy.

sources.title: Dwight's Speech
sources.note: A question reduced to yes or no, asking whether an insult is part of the advice, announcements delivered as alarming bulletins, a title asserted over colleagues, and a rally-style speech wildly out of proportion.

sources.title: Drug Testing
sources.note: A volunteer law-enforcement title invoked constantly, a search warrant explained step by step, company policy cited as law, and friendships counted with exceptions.

sources.title: Money
sources.note: A hospitality pitch for an unusual business, odd features and themed rooms listed proudly, review sites called the lifeblood of the industry, and alarming details offered as amenities.

sources.title: What's your favorite Dwight quote?
sources.note: The lines fans remember from the whole series: his alarming facts, rules and defensive add-ons.

sources.title: What's your all time favorite Dwight quote?
sources.note: A second fan collection, cross-checking the wording of the best-known lines.

observations.trait: Titles and credentials come first and are invoked as authority for everything.
Questions are answered literally and reduced to their logical options.
Next steps are explained as official procedure, with policy cited as law.
Pitches list features proudly, odd ones included, in a hospitality professional's voice.
Unnecessary, alarming details and defensive add-ons close the line, and any stage brings grand rhetoric.
A choice reduced to logic: "Whenever I'm about to do something, I think, 'Would an idiot do that?' And if they would, I do not do that thing."
An alarming fact about himself, deadpan: "Through concentration, I can raise and lower my cholesterol at will."
A last line that makes it worse: "Fortunately, my feelings regenerate at twice the speed of a normal man's."
Rhetoric wildly out of proportion: "I am ready to face any challenges that might be foolish enough to face me."

illustration.brief: After eight months of building, we launch our app on Friday. It turns voice notes into a to-do list. Free for the first month.
illustration.text: Attention. As of Friday, our app is operational. Development time: eight months. You speak. It converts your voice notes into a to-do list. That is the procedure. It does not get bored, and it does not ask how your weekend was. The first month is free, per launch policy. Those who do not download it will be noted.
